discrepancies.claim: license_spdx MIT for the listed files
discrepancies.finding: GitHub license API at the pinned SHA returns key 'other' / spdx NOASSERTION. The LICENSE text applies MIT to everything except directories NEURON_ORIG and NEURON_MODIFIED, whose code is provided on condition of citing the ModelDB entry and original publication (CITATION.md). Every listed .mep file (NEURON_MODIFIED/.test.*.spikes.mep) is inside the carve-out, so it is not MIT-licensed; no open license is stated for it. The candidate 'concerns' mention the carve-out, but the rationale line 'All NeuroML2 files sit outside those folders' does not cover the .mep files that are in the file list.
discrepancies.recommendation: Record the per-file license: NeuroML2/* = MIT; NEURON_MODIFIED/*.mep = citation-condition only. Either do not vendor the .mep files (regenerate NeuroSem's own reference traces in M2) or vendor them with the required citation and a note that no redistribution license is granted.

discrepancies.severity: high (for a pure-Python or Java-free path); informational if jNeuroML is the frozen simulator
discrepancies.claim: LTS executes; only XSD validity is at issue
discrepancies.finding: PyLEMS 0.6.9 (pylems -nogui -I <NeuroML2CoreTypes at NeuroML2 a5f5dad> LEMS_LTS.xml) parses and builds the model, then raises ZeroDivisionError in a generated update_state_variables function within about 1 s of starting the run, and writes no output. Inferred cause (unverified): IT_s_gate extends gateHHtauInf, whose Dynamics include TimeDerivative q' = (inf - q)/tau; the IT s gate sets tau to 0 (fixedTimeCourse tau='0ms' and DerivedVariable tau=0), and PyLEMS appears to keep the parent's TimeDerivative. jNeuroML runs it (CI py3.12 jNeuroML log: LTS spike and Ca-spike observables passed).
discrepancies.recommendation: If LTS is kept, NeuroSem must name jNeuroML (Java) as both the validity oracle (jnml -validate) and the execution oracle, and M1 must install Java in the frozen environment. The strict libNeuroML XSD check and PyLEMS cannot serve as fallbacks for LTS or its mutants.

discrepancies.claim: Custom LEMS ComponentTypes are in IT (LTS) and IL (IB)
discrepancies.finding: Ca.nml, which both LTS and IB include, also defines a custom ComponentType (decayingPoolConcentrationModelPosp). libNeuroML still reports Ca.nml VALID, but mutation and transformation tooling must parse LEMS Dynamics in Ca.nml as well as IT/IL. IL.channel.nml defines four custom rate ComponentTypes (IL_q_alpha_rate, IL_q_beta_rate, IL_r_alpha_rate, IL_r_beta_rate).
discrepancies.recommendation: List Ca.nml's custom ComponentType in the LTS concerns.

IT.channel.nml, Ca.nml and IL.channel.nml declare encoding ISO-8859-1 in the XML prolog, but contain zero non-ASCII bytes, so the content is plain ASCII and is byte-identical under UTF-8. This is a declaration quirk, not a practical encoding hazard. The 'K channels' isVersionOf annotation on the Ca channel IT is confirmed.
discrepancies.recommendation: Reword to 'declares ISO-8859-1; content is ASCII'. Tools that rewrite XML should preserve or normalise the declaration deliberately (a valid-transformation candidate).

discrepancies.claim: The docs.neuroml.org single-compartment HH page attributes the model to Hodgkin & Huxley 1952
discrepancies.finding: The page (HTTP 200) cites [HH52] for the HH neuron it builds with a pyNeuroML script. It does not mention NML2_SingleCompHHCell.nml or LEMS_NML2_Ex5_DetCell.xml, so applying that attribution to this specific file is an inference. The HH 1952 citation itself is confirmed by Crossref (DOI 10.1113/jphysiol.1952.sp004764) and PubMed 12991237. The candidate's citation_url is a Crossref query URL rather than a works/<doi> URL.
discrepancies.recommendation: Use https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1113/jphysiol.1952.sp004764 and describe the file as a textbook HH implementation in the NeuroML2 spec repo.
